newsitem.title: USA: Chase eyes growth in merchant processing.
newsitem.headline: Chase eyes growth in merchant processing.

text.p: Chase Manhattan Corp believes a robust growth rate and new technologies make the merchant processing business attractive and the quickest way to get involved is through a joint venture, a Chase executive said Monday.

"From Chase's perspective we felt that this was the way to get back into the business," Gary Roboff, senior vice president of Chase Manhattan, said in a telephone interview. "It's really the way we could achieve the kind of scale we wanted to achieve early on."
Chase and First Data Corp said in a joint press release they were forming a joint venture in merchant processing.

Neither company would discuss financial terms of the venture. Chase will provide clearing and settlement for the joint venture while first Data will provide merchant processing services and back office operations, with both companies contributing to the sales and marketing effort.

The venture will be known as Chase Merchant Services. The companies said the venture is expected to get under way in the first quarter of 1997 with services to merchants for credit, debit and stored value transaction cards.

The three predecessor banks of Chase Manhattan -- Chemical Banking Corp, the old Chase Manhattan and Manufacturers Hanover Trust -- all had been in processing in the 1980s. Each of the banks withdrew for various reasons.
Roboff said that the business is now electronic-based unlike in the 1980's when a big portion was paper-based.
"Today it's virtually all electronic," he said. "That's one of the things that makes it very attractive to us."
Roboff said a 20 percent annual growth rate also makes the merchant processing business attractive. He also cited opportunities presented by new technologies.
"We look forward to this venture playing a strong role on the Internet," he said. He added that Chase will be able to bring value-added capabilities to business-to-business transactions.

Alan Boyer, a spokesman for First Data, said his company has alliances with other banks including NationsBank Corp . He said First Data finds it desirable to enter into the partnerships because the banks can offer an array of financial services.
Robert McNamara, formerly president of First Data Client Merchant Services, will become chief executive officer of Chase Merchant Services.

The companies said Chase Merchant Services will have an initial portfolio of nearly $90 billion in annual credit, debit and card sales volume from 30,000 merchant accounts. They said it will rank as the largest U.S. merchant processing business.
